questions.stem: Why can DNA not leave the nucleus to reach the ribosomes directly?

options.text: DNA does not contain the genetic code
DNA molecules are too large to pass through the nuclear pores
DNA would be destroyed by enzymes in the cytoplasm
DNA is too small to find the ribosomes

questions.explanation: DNA molecules are very large and cannot pass through the nuclear pores. Instead, a smaller mRNA copy of the code is made, which can travel through the pores to the ribosomes.
